title: Verb Patterns: Gerunds and Infinitives
summary: Choose -ing forms or to-infinitives after common verbs, adjectives and prepositions.

explanation.heading: Gerunds after certain verbs
explanation.body: Some verbs, such as enjoy, avoid and suggest, are usually followed by an -ing form.
explanation.example: I enjoy learning new programming languages.

explanation.heading: To-infinitives after certain verbs
explanation.body: Verbs such as decide, agree and want are typically followed by to + base verb.
explanation.example: We decided to redesign the interface.

explanation.heading: After prepositions
explanation.body: When a verb follows a preposition, use its -ing form. The to in look forward to is a preposition, not an infinitive marker.
explanation.example: I look forward to hearing from you.

exercises.feedback: Enjoy is normally followed by the -ing form.
Decide is followed by a to-infinitive.

exercises.prompt: I'm looking forward to ___ from you.
exercises.feedback: Look forward to ends in a preposition, followed by a gerund.
Agree is followed by a to-infinitive.
A verb following the preposition in takes the -ing form.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: They suggested to postpone the meeting.
exercises.feedback: Suggest can be followed by a gerund: suggested postponing.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I want learning more about FPGAs.
exercises.feedback: Want is followed by a to-infinitive.
acceptedAnswers: I want to learn more about FPGAs.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: She is good at to explain complex ideas.
acceptedAnswers: She is good at explaining complex ideas.

exercises.feedback: Postpone is followed by a gerund.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I look forward to discuss the results.
acceptedAnswers: I look forward to discussing the results.
exercises.feedback: Look forward to is followed by a gerund.

learningObjectives: Identify common verbs followed by -ing or to-infinitive.
Use -ing after prepositions, including look forward to.

left.label: Verb + -ing
left.note: Enjoy is followed by the -ing form.

right.label: Verb + to-infinitive
right.example: We decided to redesign the board.
right.note: Decide is followed by to + base verb.

left.label: Infinitive marker
left.note: To is part of the infinitive.

examples.sentence: She avoided making the same mistake.
They agreed to test the new firmware.
He is interested in learning more.
examples.note: Prepositions such as in take a noun or -ing form.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I suggest to review the code.
commonMistakes.why: Suggest is normally followed by -ing when there is no object clause.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I am looking forward to meet you.
commonMistakes.correct: I am looking forward to meeting you.
commonMistakes.why: To in this expression is a preposition.

studyTips: Learn verb patterns together with a complete phrase, not as isolated rules.
For verbs whose meaning changes with the complement, study each usage separately.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that you enjoy solving problems.
speakingExercises.feedback: Enjoy is followed by a gerund.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that you decided to study English.
speakingExercises.feedback: Decide is followed by to + infinitive.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that you avoid working late.
speakingExercises.feedback: Avoid is followed by an -ing form.

listeningExercises.feedback: Enjoy is followed by an -ing form.

listeningExercises.audioText: We decided to redesign the board.
listeningExercises.feedback: Decide is normally followed by a to-infinitive.

listeningExercises.audioText: She avoided making the same mistake.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the -ing form you hear after “avoided”.
